## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** Which statement gives the grain of the SalesInvoiceLine fact table?

A.  One line of one invoice
B.  One invoice with its total
C.  One item in one fiscal quarter
D.  One customer in one month

**2.** In the model of Chapter 13, Customer filters SalesInvoice, and SalesInvoice filters SalesInvoiceLine. In the terms of this chapter, what is this arrangement?

A.  A star with two fact tables that share the Customer dimension
B.  A many-to-many relationship that runs through a junction table
C.  A snowflake, with Customer reached through the header
D.  A degenerate dimension stored inside the invoice line fact table

**3.** After the header is flattened into the lines, InvoiceNumber stays in SalesInvoiceLine and is used to filter and group, with no table of its own. What is it called?

A.  A role-playing dimension
B.  A degenerate dimension
C.  A calculated table
D.  A surrogate key

**4.** A colleague sets the relationship between Date and SalesInvoiceLine to Both, so that a date slicer lists only the days with sales. In the model of this chapter, what is the main risk?

A.  The Date table can no longer be marked as the model's date table
B.  The relationship becomes inactive until a measure switches it on
C.  Every measure that uses DIVIDE begins to return an error
D.  A selection on Item can then filter the ledger through Date

**5.** SalesInvoiceLine has an InvoiceDate and a ShipmentDate, and the Date table is related to both. How does a measure calculate revenue by ship date?

A.  By setting the ship-date relationship to Both
B.  By adding a second date table filtered with FILTER
C.  By using USERELATIONSHIP inside CALCULATE
D.  By sorting Date by the ShipmentDate column

**6.** The Charles River ledger runs from January 1, 2024, into February 2027. Which date table follows Microsoft's guidance?

A.  One row for each day from January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2027
B.  One row for each invoice date that appears in the invoice lines
C.  One row for each month from January 2024 to February 2027
D.  One row for each day from January 1, 2024, through February 23, 2027

**7.** Which of the following belongs in a measure rather than in a calculated column?

A.  The product type taken from the code of each item
B.  The margin percentage of each cell in a matrix
C.  The list amount of each invoice line
D.  A flag on each posting of a closing entry

**8.** The invoice lines hold the quantity, and the Item table holds the standard cost per unit. How should a measure calculate the standard cost of the lines in the filter context?

A.  Multiply the total quantity by the total of the items' standard costs
B.  Multiply the total quantity by the average standard cost of all items
C.  Use RELATED in the measure itself, without an iterator around it
D.  Iterate the lines with SUMX, multiplying quantity by RELATED cost

**9.** A matrix shows revenue by item group on rows and by quarter on columns, and a slicer on the page is set to the Wholesale segment. Which filters make up the filter context of the Furniture cell for 2026-Q4?

A.  Only the item group and the quarter of the cell's row and column
B.  The item group, the quarter, and the Wholesale segment
C.  Only the slicer, because rows and columns group without filtering
D.  None, because measures ignore filters unless CALCULATE is used

**10.** In a calculated column on the Customer table, `SUM ( SalesInvoiceLine[LineTotal] )` returns the same large amount on every row. Why?

A.  The relationship from Customer to the invoice lines is inactive
B.  Calculated columns are evaluated before relationships exist
C.  SUM ignores relationships unless its column is hidden
D.  The row context does not filter the lines without CALCULATE

**11.** A table visual by item group shows the measure `CALCULATE ( [Revenue], 'Item'[ItemGroup] = "Furniture" )`. What does the Lighting row show?

A.  Furniture's revenue, because the filter replaces Lighting
B.  Lighting's revenue, because the row's filter takes priority
C.  A blank, because the two item groups cannot both apply
D.  Zero, because the two filters on ItemGroup intersect

**12.** A share measure divides the revenue of each item group by `CALCULATE ( [Revenue], ALL ( SalesInvoiceLine ) )`. With a year slicer set to 2026, Furniture's share reads about a fifth. What is wrong?

A.  ALL ignores the relationship between Item and the invoice lines
B.  DIVIDE rounds its result down whenever a slicer is applied
C.  Removing the filters from the fact table also removes the year
D.  A share should be calculated with AVERAGE instead of DIVIDE

**13.** What makes a query in the Tests tab of DAX query view a useful test of the model?

A.  It runs faster than the visuals that show the same measures on a page
B.  Its result is compared with a control total from another source
C.  It is saved in a separate file that the report cannot change
D.  It replaces the measure in every visual of the report

**14.** A matrix by year shows `CALCULATE ( [Revenue], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) )` next to Revenue. Which year shows a prior-year value but no revenue?

A.  2024, because the data begins in January 2024
B.  2025, because 2024 was a start-up year
C.  2027, because the date table runs through 2027
D.  None, because the function skips years without data

**15.** An income statement built on all the postings to the revenue and expense accounts shows a net income of zero in every year. What explains it?

A.  The year-end closes reverse each year's revenue and expenses
B.  Revenue is stored as credits, which cancel the debits of the expenses
C.  The Date table is not marked, so the years are not kept apart
D.  The relationship between GLEntry and Account is set to Both
